subject.title: [Feature]: Mobile apps: per-gateway custom headers for gateways behind authenticating proxies

question: Should the mobile Gateway clients support arbitrary per-gateway custom headers, or should owner/security review narrow this to typed proxy-auth fields before the Android and iOS PRs land?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior stores and replays credentials before OpenClaw Gateway auth, so automation should not choose the permanent security and UX contract.

options.title: Approve Guarded Custom Headers
options.body: Land per-platform custom-header support only after owner/security review confirms secure storage, redaction, reserved-header sanitization, gateway-only attachment, and real proxy proof.

options.title: Narrow To Typed Proxy Auth
options.body: Ask the platform PRs to expose only specific Basic, Bearer, or service-token fields first, reducing arbitrary header risk at the cost of some operator flexibility.

options.title: Defer Mobile Proxy Credentials
options.body: Keep native mobile proxy-header support out of scope for now and document VPN, tunnel, WebChat, or proxy-bypass alternatives.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Custom Headers
recommendation.body: Land per-platform custom-header support only after owner/security review confirms secure storage, redaction, reserved-header sanitization, gateway-only attachment, and real proxy proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the issue and the linked platform PRs and has the clearest current signal across mobile gateway auth and security/product scope.
